body:
P2-12 PLAN 5/6: EVERY CALL THE PHONE MAKES TODAY FOR THE CATALOGUE (file:line, main 346883b) AND WHERE IT GOES
The client app/lib/data/catalogue/deezer_client.dart: base address api.deezer.com line 15; search artist, album, track (three at once) 55 to 57; searchArtists 74; artist 80; album 86; artist top 93; artist albums 103; chart tracks, artists, albums 113 to 115; album tracks 129 and 133 (the album again for its cover). Built at features/requests/request_providers.dart:27 (CachedCatalogueClient(DeezerClient())) and app/background_sync.dart:90 (catalogue ?? DeezerClient(): the background isolate bypasses every provider). Callers:
- request_providers.dart:224 (catalogueSearchProvider) and :227 (withArtistSongs -> artist_aware_search.dart:96 searchArtists, :99 artistTopTracks: up to 6 artist searches and 2 top lists per typed query on top of the 3 of the search) -> search and artists/{id}?parts=popular in slice 2; the artist + title reading, the padding filter (matchesQueryWords), rankNamesakes and the ownership ids move into the server's search in slice 6.
- catalogue_providers.dart:25 album, :29 albumTracks -> albums/{id}; :33 artist, :42 artistTop, :202 artistAlbums -> artists/{id}; :38 genreChart -> genres/{id} (genre_screen.dart:61; the list kCatalogueGenres moves to GET genres).
- catalogue_providers.dart:166 searchArtists and :183 artistAlbums (up to 3 at once): the N-14 chain -> catalogue/artist, slice 3.
- features/common/open_artist.dart:45 -> search types=artists in slice 2, the identity in slice 6.
- features/settings/import_screen.dart:578 (the second import screen; P2-07 deletes it) -> search.
- features/detail/album_gap.dart:62 search and :72 albumTracks -> albums/match, slice 6.
- data/repos/cover_fallback_repository.dart:89 (a cover for an album the server has no cover for; it duplicates in the phone what the server's cover finder does for songs) -> albums/match with tracks=0, slice 6.
- data/alerts/alerts_service.dart:326 search and :344 artistAlbums, run from background_sync (every 20 hours, 15 watched artists) -> slice 6: AlertsService gets a client made from the session background_sync already builds (session.encoreApi) and asks the library-artist route; its identity map goes. This is itself a stop-gap: P2-15 moves the whole release check to the server (trigger: P2-15 merged, then AlertsService._releases is deleted). Plain servers get no release alerts (D1).
- features/instant/instant_warmup.dart:13 and :22, features/jam/add_songs_sheet.dart:66 -> follow the providers.
OUTSIDE ADDRESSES THAT ARE DATA and stay after P2-12 (the ratchet cannot see them, docs/30 section 5): catalogue pictures (cdn-images.dzcdn.net in cover and picture fields, drawn by CachedNetworkImage in features/common/cover_art.dart), YouTube thumbnails (i.ytimg.com, P1-26), the lyrics client (lrclib_client.dart:13, P2-14). PRIVACY.md (B-88) must say in slice 1: what the server sends to Deezer (the typed text and ids, from the server's address, not the phone's) and that phones still fetch pictures from Deezer's picture host. A later item "catalogue pictures come through your server" (signed route, host allow-list, disk cache; the last row of the ADR-R38 table) closes it; the new shapes keep picture fields as plain strings so that switch changes their value, not their place.
STAYS ON THE PHONE: the offline search of the library (FTS: search_dao.dart, app_database.dart:110, the N-23a artist_typo scan); the join of a catalogue row with a row of the phone's own database (LibraryMatcher, text_match.dart: a matcher only for what is on the phone, B-46); the merge and scoring of library and catalogue rows (search_assembly.dart, search_rank.dart: ONE ranker, on the phone, until the server's ranked list in P2-12b; slice 2 must not change a ranking, which the 20 recorded searches prove); the 30-minute view memory CachedCatalogueClient (written to sit in front of whichever client answers: a phone cache, not a stop-gap); the drawing.
